representations.text: Over 28 baseline days and 14 window days with complete wear, all metrics remained highly stable. Sleep duration averaged ~471 min (baseline) vs ~472 min (window), consistently ending at 07:00 with starts near 22:50. Steps (~7938 vs ~7923), activity (~55 vs ~56 min), low movement (~450 vs ~447 min), resting HR (~61.8 vs ~61.7 bpm), and RMSSD (~44.8 vs ~45.1 ms) showed negligible shifts. Weekday/weekend patterns were similar across periods. Paired correlations between activity and next-day sleep, steps and activity, and RHR and RMSSD were weak in both periods. No sustained directional changes occurred.

Across 28 baseline and 14 window days with full wear, most metrics stayed stable. Sleep averaged ~471 min (baseline) vs ~468 min (window), always ending at 07:00; sleep start shifted ~3 min later. Steps (~8066 vs ~7954), activity (~55 min both), low movement (~451 vs ~453 min), and resting HR (~56.3 vs ~55.8 bpm) changed minimally. However, RMSSD dropped from a stable ~45.3 ms to ~43.1 ms, driven by an isolated value of 23 ms on Apr 5 that returned to 43 ms the next day; excluding it, window RMSSD was ~44.6 ms. Paired correlations remained weak throughout.

During the 28-day baseline, metrics were stable with full wear: sleep ~471 min ending at 07:00, steps ~7998, activity ~55 min, low movement ~451 min, resting HR ~56.1 bpm, and RMSSD ~45.3 ms. In the 14-day window, steps fell abruptly to ~2321/day (−71%) and activity to ~5 min/day (from ~55 min), persisting throughout. Sleep remained near ~469 min with unchanged timing. Low movement (~448 min), resting HR (~56.3 bpm), and RMSSD (~44.8 ms) were stable. The step and activity reductions were continuous without recovery; other metrics were unaffected.

Over 28 baseline days with complete wear, metrics were stable: sleep ~471 min ending exactly at 07:00 daily, steps ~7938, activity ~55 min, low movement ~450 min, resting HR ~51.8 bpm, and RMSSD ~44.8 ms. In the 14-day window, resting HR rose abruptly to ~61.7 bpm (+10 bpm, +19%) from day one and persisted throughout. All other metrics remained near baseline levels: sleep ~472 min, steps ~7923, activity ~56 min, low movement ~447 min, and RMSSD ~45.1 ms. Sleep timing, weekday/weekend structure, and paired correlations were unchanged. The HR shift was sustained without return toward baseline.
